newsitem.title: USA: Norfolk lawyer mum on meetings by rail CEOs.
newsitem.headline: Norfolk lawyer mum on meetings by rail CEOs.

text.p: A lawyer for Norfolk Southern Corp declined to comment Tuesday when asked whether the chief executives of Conrail Inc, Norfolk Southern and CSX Corp have had any further summit meetings over the proposed merger of Conrail and CSX.

Conrail's David LeVan, Norfolk Southern's David Goode and CSX's John Snow met on January 31 in their first effort to bridge the gap created between all three companies after Norfolk Southern's $115-per-share hostile tender offer for Conrail's stock, which has a value about $10.3 billion, nearly $1 billion higher than CSX's cash-and-stock offer.
"I think it would be inappropriate for me to comment on that," the lawyer, Steven Rothschild, said after a federal court hearing.
The federal Third Circuit Court of Appeals heard Norfolk Southern's appeal of a lower-court ruling that declined to block key provisions of the proposed merger between Conrail and CSX.
A news blackout was imposed by the companies, who said they would not disclose any details about the Janaury 31 meeting or any subsequent meetings, if there were any.
The other attorneys were not immediately available to comment on the question, and none of the rail executives attended the appelate hearing.
